hypothesis: Humans shed their front teeth, no species in the eruption table sheds molars, and the pig sheds no teeth.
pass_criterion: Supports only if all three clauses hold. (1) Humans shed front teeth: primary incisors are described as erupted and later replaced or shed. (2) No animal sheds molars: the eruption table lists no deciduous molar for any species. (3) The pig sheds none of its teeth: the pig has no deciduous incisor, canine or premolar with an eruption time.
fail_criterion: Refutes if clause 3 fails and clause 2 fails. Mixed if clause 3 fails and clause 2 holds, or if clause 3 holds and clause 2 fails. Clause 1 is reported either way and does not by itself change a mixed or refutes verdict reached from clauses 2 and 3. Inconclusive, reason data-unavailable, if the pig row cannot be parsed. A deciduous tooth with a later permanent successor of the same class counts as shed. Permanent molars with no deciduous predecessor count as not shed.

test_contract.expected_observation: The pig column has no deciduous teeth, no species has a deciduous molar, and humans replace primary incisors.
test_contract.disconfirming_observation: The pig has at least one deciduous tooth class, or any species has a deciduous molar.
test_contract.admissible_datasets: A public eruption table for domestic mammals that separates deciduous and permanent teeth, and a public human primary-dentition account. The table's species are the animals tested for the molar clause; elephants and other species absent from the table are outside this measurement and are stated as a caveat, not added after the fact.
test_contract.inference_method: Parse deciduous rows (incisors, canines, premolars, molars) against permanent successors. Clause 3 fails if the pig has any deciduous eruption. Clause 2 fails if any species has a deciduous molar. Supports only if all three clauses hold. The pig clause failing while molars are not shed is mixed; both failing is refutes.

interpretation: The sentence has three clauses: man sheds his front teeth; no animal sheds its molars; the pig sheds none at all. 'Molars' are the permanent molar positions, not the deciduous premolars sometimes called milk molars. 'Sheds' means a deciduous tooth is replaced by a later permanent tooth. The pig is Sus scrofa.

deviations.change: The human clause was read from OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e section 23.3.
deviations.why: The NCBI Bookshelf URL returned a browser-check page. Pass and fail thresholds were not changed. Clause 1 does not decide a mixed or refutes verdict on its own.

method: The Merck eruption table lists deciduous incisors, canines and premolars separately from permanent molars. A deciduous cell with an eruption age counts as a tooth that is shed when its permanent successor erupts. The pig sheds teeth if any such cell is filled. No species sheds molars if the table has no deciduous-molar row. OpenStax says the deciduous teeth are replaced and that the incisors are the front teeth; that is clause 1. Clause 3 failing while clause 2 holds is mixed, as pre-registered.

measured.unit: pig deciduous tooth classes with an eruption time

caveats: Deciduous premolars are not counted as molars. Aristotle's 'molars' might have included cheek teeth that are now called premolars; that broader reading is not the one pre-registered.
The table covers horse, cow, sheep, goat, pig, dog and cat. Elephants, which replace molars, are outside this measurement.
